column1: # Expected bindings rows for the bindings trap fixture (js-ts).
# one per line, byte-sorted. scripts/check.sh asserts this set exactly against
# <out>/bindings.tsv: a missing line is a binding the extractor stopped finding,
# an extra line is one it invented. Both are regressions.
# Written from the fixture sources and the bindings spec alone, by an
# independent oracle that never saw the extractor or its output; the two are
# reconciled separately. `to` is pinned to the edges in EXPECTED.tsv.
# Regenerate deliberately, never reflexively - the point of the file is
# that it does not move when the extractor changes.
# - src/barrel.cjs:4 module.exports = (line 3) / require("./lib/b") (line 4): unbound cjs row on line 4, the line holding require(, not the module.exports line.
# - src/lib/multiline-require.ts:6 destructured require split over lines 3-6: both rows carry line 6, the line holding require(, not the `const {` line 3.
# - src/lib/destructure.ts:4,6 defaults are not part of a name: `a = 1` -> a/a, `d: e = 2` -> e/d.
# - src/lib/destructure.ts:5 rest element `...rest`: rest/*/module/cjs (it binds an object of the module's remaining exports; there is no export named rest).
# - src/lib/calls.ts:4 require("./b").Foo and :5 require("./b")("app") are unbound cjs rows (empty local), not Foo/dbg bindings; :6 import("./b").then(...) is an unbound dynamic row.

# - src/lib/chained-calls.ts: .x on the next code line (:6), ?.x (:8), ['x'] (:9), !.x (:10) are unbound cjs rows on the require( line; :13 await import("./b") with .then(...) on line 14 is an unbound dynamic row on line 13.

# - src/lib/destructure-default.ts:8 require("./b") as the default of b in a multi-line `const {...} = obj`: one unbound cjs row on line 8 (the destructure binds from obj, not from the module); a gets no row.
# - src/lib/string-decoy.ts: require(/import( text inside string defaults is data: no row and no edge to evil.ts/evil2.ts.

# - src/lib/semicolon-string.js:6 the "import('./evil')" string is data; `const a = require('./a')` after the `;` is its own statement: a/*/module/cjs; foo() on line 7 starts a new statement (no chain).

# - src/lib/no-semicolons.js:5 `const load = () => import("./page"), cfg = require("./cfg")`: the import() is returned from an arrow, so an unbound dynamic row; cfg is a LATER declarator of the same const, and only the first declarator binds (spec), so require("./cfg") is an unbound cjs row (empty local).
# - src/lib/multiline-string-destructure.js: the 'x\<newline>y' string default and the f("require('./evil')") argument are strings: no row, no edge.
# - src/lib/require-comparison.js:5 `!== undefined` on line 6 continues the expression: require("./cfg") is compared, not bound, so an unbound cjs row on line 5 (ok gets no row).

# - src/lib/comma-and-var.js:7-9 `x, cfgN = require('./cfg')` comma-operator statements with no declaration keyword (decoys: "let's" in a string, `var` inside a function body, `opts.var`): unbound cjs rows on 7, 8, 9.

# - src/lib/comma-and-var.js:10-11 `var fs1 = require('./a'),` / `cfg4 = require('./cfg');`: fs1, the first declarator, binds (fs1/*/module/cjs, line 10); cfg4 is a later declarator: unbound cjs row on line 11, the line holding its require(.
# - src/lib/bang-iife.js:4 `!function(){}()` on line 5 does not chain onto require("./a") (spec: a `!` on the next line is a new statement): a2/*/module/cjs.
# - src/lib/types-trap.ts:6 { type as t } imports the value `type` as t (no type flag); :7 type{T} is a type-only clause; :8 import type from is a default import named type (no flag).
# - src/route-a.ts:5-6 and src/route-b.ts:6-7 one edge reached by two routes: conf is each statement's own resolution (relative EXTRACTED, no flag; @lib alias INFERRED, alias) whichever comes first.
# - src/Report.vue:5 template text "import your data from "CSV" files" is not code: no row; only the <script> import on line 12.
# - src/lib/keywords-a.ts:11, src/lib/types-trap.ts:10 local export const declarators and the export { ... } lists without from: no rows.
